title: Minimum Operations to Make the Array Beautiful
summary: Given an integer array nums, transform it into a beautiful array by ensuring that for every index i > 0, the value at nums[i] is divisible by nums[i - 1].
statement: Given an integer array nums, transform it into a beautiful array by ensuring that for every index i > 0, the value at nums[i] is divisible by nums[i - 1]. You can perform an operation by incrementing any element nums[i] (where i > 0) by 1. Determine the minimum number of such operations required to achieve the beautiful array.
constraints: nums contains one to 100 values, each between one and 50.
Only positions after index zero may be incremented.
Minimize increments so every value is divisible by its predecessor.
hints: The optimal choice at one position depends only on its adjusted predecessor.
Keep the minimum cost for every feasible adjusted value through 100 and transition to each multiple of the predecessor not below the original value.
Add exactly current-original to the prior cost and merge equal current values by minimum.
The DP enumerates every legal nondecreasing-by-increments chain; dominated costs with the same final value can never help later.
editorial: The DP enumerates every legal nondecreasing-by-increments chain; dominated costs with the same final value can never help later.

tests.explanation: Raising seven to nine costs two and yields [3,9,9].
Every adjacent divisibility condition already holds, so the cost is zero.
